panels.description: One row per Claude Code session, drawn as one solid bar in the session's own colour from its first prompt's start to its last prompt's end. A session that started before the range and was used again in it runs from the start of the range. Idle time between prompts is included, even if the session was closed and resumed. A session still running after the range ends at the end of the range. Hover a bar for the session's prompt count and tokens (input, output, cache read and cache write together) in the range, its Session Age, from its first prompt's start to its last prompt's end, and its Activity Time, the time its prompts ran for, idle time left out and overlapping prompts counted once. Session Age and Activity Time include the session's prompts from before the range, but only those the User and Repository filters and your access let you see. Grafana's own Duration in the tooltip is only the part of the bar inside the range. Shows the 30 most recently active sessions in the range. Colours are assigned in the order sessions started, so they can change with the time range or filters. Rows are labelled with the session's repository (GH:, GL: or BB: and its path, or Unknown) and the first 8 characters of its session ID. Times are shown in your browser's timezone.

targets.rawSql:
-- base is every prompt in the range the panel may show, s counts and ranks each session's prompts in
-- the range, and top keeps the 30 most recently active sessions. history and whole read those
-- sessions' prompts from before the range too, to find each session's first prompt and its Activity
-- Time. shown numbers the sessions for their colours, and the outer query turns each session into a
-- start point and an end point, so it draws as one solid bar.
WITH base AS (
  SELECT p.id, p.workspace_key, p.session_id, p.started_at, p.ended_at, p.repository_url,
    p.input_tokens + p.output_tokens + p.cache_read_tokens + p.cache_creation_tokens AS tokens
  FROM ai_prompts p
  -- Prompts that overlap the time range, so a prompt that began before the range still shows.
  -- ended_at isn't indexed, so the lower bound on started_at lets MySQL use its index. It assumes no
  -- prompt runs over 24 hours, as on Working Time.
  WHERE p.started_at >= DATE_SUB($__timeFrom(), INTERVAL 24 HOUR)
    AND p.started_at < $__timeTo() AND p.ended_at > $__timeFrom()
    -- The same filters apply in history below. Using prompts the viewer can't see would reveal
    -- their timing.
    AND p.source_connection_id IN (SELECT c_g.id FROM _tool_claude_code_otel_connections c_g JOIN _tool_claude_code_otel_connection_projects cp_g ON cp_g.connection_id = c_g.id JOIN user_project_mapping upm_g ON upm_g.project_name = cp_g.project_name WHERE c_g.status = 'active' AND upm_g.user_login = ${__user.login:sqlstring})
    -- user is single-select, so this is one user.
    AND COALESCE(NULLIF(p.user_email, ''), p.user_key) = ${user:sqlstring}
    -- '__all__' is the Repository filter's allValue: All sends it instead of the option list, so a
    -- range with no repositories can't produce IN ().
    AND ('__all__' IN (${repository:sqlstring}) OR COALESCE(p.repository_url, 'Unknown') IN (${repository:sqlstring}))
), s AS (
  SELECT workspace_key, session_id,
    MAX(repository_url) AS repository_url,
    MAX(ended_at) AS last_end,
    -- Shown in the bar's tooltip. Tokens are input, output, cache read and cache write together.
    COUNT(*) AS prompts,
    SUM(tokens) AS tokens,
    -- 1 is the session that was active most recently.
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY MAX(ended_at) DESC, workspace_key, session_id) AS recency
  FROM base
  GROUP BY workspace_key, session_id
), top AS (
  -- More rows than this can't be read in one panel, and the panel maps 30 colours. Narrow the
  -- User or Repository filter instead.
  SELECT * FROM s WHERE recency <= 30
), history AS (
  -- Each shown session's prompts that started before the range's end, including those before the
  -- range, under the same filters as base. run_end is the latest end among the session's prompts
  -- so far. A running max is computed incrementally; a frame that stops one row early is rescanned
  -- for every row.
  SELECT e.id, e.workspace_key, e.session_id, e.started_at, e.ended_at,
    MAX(e.ended_at) OVER (PARTITION BY e.workspace_key, e.session_id ORDER BY e.started_at, e.ended_at, e.id
      ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS run_end
  FROM ai_prompts e
  JOIN top ON top.workspace_key = e.workspace_key AND top.session_id = e.session_id
  WHERE e.started_at < $__timeTo()
    AND e.source_connection_id IN (SELECT c_g.id FROM _tool_claude_code_otel_connections c_g JOIN _tool_claude_code_otel_connection_projects cp_g ON cp_g.connection_id = c_g.id JOIN user_project_mapping upm_g ON upm_g.project_name = cp_g.project_name WHERE c_g.status = 'active' AND upm_g.user_login = ${__user.login:sqlstring})
    AND COALESCE(NULLIF(e.user_email, ''), e.user_key) = ${user:sqlstring}
    AND ('__all__' IN (${repository:sqlstring}) OR COALESCE(e.repository_url, 'Unknown') IN (${repository:sqlstring}))
), gaps AS (
  -- prev_end is the latest end among the session's earlier prompts.
  SELECT history.*,
    LAG(run_end) OVER (PARTITION BY workspace_key, session_id ORDER BY started_at, ended_at, id) AS prev_end
  FROM history
), whole AS (
  -- first_start is the session's first prompt. Activity Time counts only the part of each prompt
  -- after the session's earlier prompts ended, so time when prompts overlap is counted once.
  SELECT workspace_key, session_id, MIN(started_at) AS first_start,
    ROUND(SUM(GREATEST(0, TIMESTAMPDIFF(MICROSECOND, GREATEST(started_at, COALESCE(prev_end, started_at)), ended_at))) / 1000000) AS activity_seconds
  FROM gaps
  GROUP BY workspace_key, session_id
), shown AS (
  -- colour numbers the shown sessions 1, 2, 3… in the order they started; each number maps to
  -- its own colour in the panel's value mappings.
  SELECT top.*, w.first_start, w.activity_seconds,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY w.first_start, top.workspace_key, top.session_id) AS colour,
    -- The bar covers only the range: a session that began before it starts at the range's start,
    -- and one still running after it ends at the range's end.
    GREATEST(w.first_start, $__timeFrom()) AS bar_start,
    LEAST(top.last_end, $__timeTo()) AS bar_end,
    -- Session Age runs from the session's first prompt's start to its last prompt's end.
    ROUND(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MICROSECOND, w.first_start, top.last_end) / 1000000) AS age_seconds,
    -- The repository is labelled as on the Claude Prompts dashboards: GH:, GL: or BB: and the path,
    -- or the host for other servers.
    CONCAT(CASE
        WHEN top.repository_url IS NULL THEN 'Unknown'
        WHEN top.repository_url REGEXP '^https?://([^/]*[.])?github[^/.]*[.][^/]+/' THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(top.repository_url, '^https?://[^/]+/', 'GH: ')
        WHEN top.repository_url REGEXP '^https?://([^/]*[.])?gitlab[^/.]*[.][^/]+/' THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(top.repository_url, '^https?://[^/]+/', 'GL: ')
        WHEN top.repository_url REGEXP '^https?://(www[.])?bitbucket[.]org/' THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(top.repository_url, '^https?://[^/]+/', 'BB: ')
        -- Bitbucket Server clone URLs carry an scm/ prefix that the SSH remote of the same repository lacks.
        WHEN top.repository_url REGEXP '^https?://([^/]*[.])?bitbucket[^/.]*[.][^/]+/' THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(top.repository_url, '^https?://[^/]+/(scm/)?', 'BB: ')
        ELSE REGEXP_REPLACE(top.repository_url, '^https?://', '')
      END, ' · ', LEFT(top.session_id, 8)) AS session_label
  FROM top
  JOIN whole w ON w.workspace_key = top.workspace_key AND w.session_id = top.session_id
)
SELECT t AS time, session_label AS session, state
FROM (
  -- state is "<colour number>|<tooltip text>": the panel's regex mappings colour the bar by the number
  -- and show the text, the session's prompt count, tokens, Session Age and Activity Time, in the tooltip.
  -- Durations of a day or more show days and hours only.
  SELECT bar_start AS t, 0 AS kind, session_label,
    CONCAT(colour, '|', prompts, IF(prompts = 1, ' prompt', ' prompts'), ' · ',
      CASE
        WHEN tokens >= 1000000000 THEN CONCAT(ROUND(tokens / 1000000000, 1), 'B')
        WHEN tokens >= 1000000 THEN CONCAT(ROUND(tokens / 1000000, 1), 'M')
        WHEN tokens >= 1000 THEN CONCAT(ROUND(tokens / 1000, 1), 'K')
        ELSE tokens
      END, ' tokens · Session Age ', CASE
        WHEN age_seconds >= 86400 THEN CONCAT(FLOOR(age_seconds / 86400), 'd ', FLOOR(MOD(age_seconds, 86400) / 3600), 'h')
        WHEN age_seconds >= 3600 THEN CONCAT(FLOOR(age_seconds / 3600), 'h ', FLOOR(MOD(age_seconds, 3600) / 60), 'm')
        WHEN age_seconds >= 60 THEN CONCAT(FLOOR(age_seconds / 60), 'm ', MOD(age_seconds, 60), 's')
        ELSE CONCAT(age_seconds, 's')
      END,
      ' · Activity Time ', CASE
        WHEN activity_seconds >= 86400 THEN CONCAT(FLOOR(activity_seconds / 86400), 'd ', FLOOR(MOD(activity_seconds, 86400) / 3600), 'h')
        WHEN activity_seconds >= 3600 THEN CONCAT(FLOOR(activity_seconds / 3600), 'h ', FLOOR(MOD(activity_seconds, 3600) / 60), 'm')
        WHEN activity_seconds >= 60 THEN CONCAT(FLOOR(activity_seconds / 60), 'm ', MOD(activity_seconds, 60), 's')
        ELSE CONCAT(activity_seconds, 's')
      END) AS state
  FROM shown
  UNION ALL
  -- After the bar's end the state is NULL, so the row shows nothing until the range ends.
  SELECT bar_end, 1, session_label, NULL
  FROM shown
) pts
ORDER BY t, kind

list.definition:
-- '__none__' keeps the result from being empty, which Grafana treats as an error; the regex hides it.
-- The label is the person's full name from their DevLake account, falling back to the email; the value stays the
-- email (or user key) that every panel filters on.
SELECT COALESCE(u.full_name, u.user) AS __text, u.user AS __value
FROM (
  SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(p.user_email, ''), p.user_key) AS user,
    MAX(NULLIF(TRIM(a.full_name), '')) AS full_name
  FROM ai_prompts p
  LEFT JOIN accounts a ON a.id = p.account_id
  WHERE p.source_connection_id IN (SELECT c_g.id FROM _tool_claude_code_otel_connections c_g JOIN _tool_claude_code_otel_connection_projects cp_g ON cp_g.connection_id = c_g.id JOIN user_project_mapping upm_g ON upm_g.project_name = cp_g.project_name WHERE c_g.status = 'active' AND upm_g.user_login = ${__user.login:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY 1
  UNION ALL SELECT '__none__', NULL
) u
-- The viewer's own email sorts first, so the dashboard opens on their sessions.
ORDER BY u.user = ${__user.email:sqlstring} DESC, 1;

list.definition:
-- '__none__' keeps the result from being empty, which Grafana treats as an error; the regex hides it.
-- Repositories the selected user's prompts ran in during the time range, labelled as on Token Usage by Repository.
-- A prompt counts when it overlaps the range, as on the Session Timeline panel, so a prompt that began
-- before the range still lists its repository.
-- 'Unknown' stands for prompts without a repository; a real repository_url is always an
-- https URL, so it cannot clash.
SELECT CASE
    WHEN r.url = 'Unknown' THEN 'Unknown'
    WHEN r.url REGEXP '^https?://([^/]*[.])?github[^/.]*[.][^/]+/' THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(r.url, '^https?://[^/]+/', 'GH: ')
    WHEN r.url REGEXP '^https?://([^/]*[.])?gitlab[^/.]*[.][^/]+/' THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(r.url, '^https?://[^/]+/', 'GL: ')
    WHEN r.url REGEXP '^https?://(www[.])?bitbucket[.]org/' THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(r.url, '^https?://[^/]+/', 'BB: ')
    -- Bitbucket Server clone URLs carry an scm/ prefix that the SSH remote of the same repository lacks.
    WHEN r.url REGEXP '^https?://([^/]*[.])?bitbucket[^/.]*[.][^/]+/' THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(r.url, '^https?://[^/]+/(scm/)?', 'BB: ')
    ELSE REGEXP_REPLACE(r.url, '^https?://', '')
  END AS __text, r.url AS __value
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT COALESCE(p.repository_url, 'Unknown') AS url
  FROM ai_prompts p
  WHERE p.source_connection_id IN (SELECT c_g.id FROM _tool_claude_code_otel_connections c_g JOIN _tool_claude_code_otel_connection_projects cp_g ON cp_g.connection_id = c_g.id JOIN user_project_mapping upm_g ON upm_g.project_name = cp_g.project_name WHERE c_g.status = 'active' AND upm_g.user_login = ${__user.login:sqlstring})
    AND ('__all__' IN (${user:sqlstring}) OR COALESCE(NULLIF(p.user_email, ''), p.user_key) IN (${user:sqlstring}))
    -- ended_at isn't indexed, so the lower bound on started_at lets MySQL use its index. It assumes
    -- no prompt runs over 24 hours, as on Working Time.
    AND p.started_at >= DATE_SUB($__timeFrom(), INTERVAL 24 HOUR)
    AND p.started_at < $__timeTo() AND p.ended_at > $__timeFrom()
  UNION SELECT '__none__'
) r
ORDER BY r.url = 'Unknown', 1;
